_comment: Asset classes offered by the calculator. recovery_years is the GDS recovery period; method is the GDS method the percentage tables embody; table_family picks the Pub. 946 table set; ads_years is used for listed property at 50% or less business use. Every entry is traceable to Pub. 946.

computers.label: Computers and office equipment
computers.note: Computers and peripheral equipment (asset class 00.12) and office machinery such as copiers and calculators.
computers.source_citation: IRS Pub. 946 (2025), ch. 4 '5-year property' (d. office machinery) and Appendix B, Table B-1, asset class 00.12

furniture.label: Office furniture and fixtures
furniture.note: Desks, files, safes and similar (asset class 00.11). Furniture used in a residential rental activity is 5-year property - choose 'Other' with 5 years.
furniture.source_citation: IRS Pub. 946 (2025), ch. 4 '7-year property' (a. office furniture and fixtures)

machinery.label: Machinery and equipment
machinery.note: Seven years is the class for property with no class life and for most general business equipment. Some industries' machinery has a different class life (Pub. 946 Table B-2) - use 'Other' if yours does.
machinery.source_citation: IRS Pub. 946 (2025), ch. 4 '7-year property' (d. property without a class life) and Appendix B

qip.label: Qualified improvement property
qip.note: Interior improvements to nonresidential buildings placed in service after the building, excluding enlargements, elevators/escalators and the internal structural framework. 15-year straight line.
qip.source_citation: IRS Pub. 946 (2025), ch. 4 '15-year property' (h.) and Table 4-1 (GDS using SL: qualified improvement property); IRC 179(f)

passenger_vehicle.label: Passenger vehicle (6,000 lb GVWR or less)
passenger_vehicle.note: Listed property subject to the section 280F annual depreciation limits.
passenger_vehicle.source_citation: IRS Pub. 946 (2025), ch. 4 '5-year property' (a. automobiles) and ch. 5 (passenger automobile: 6,000 pounds or less GVWR)

heavy_vehicle.label: Heavy SUV, truck or van (over 6,000 lb GVWR)
heavy_vehicle.note: Not subject to the 280F limits, but an SUV rated 6,001-14,000 lb has a separate section 179 cap unless it seats more than nine behind the driver, has a cargo bed of at least six feet not readily accessible from the passenger area, or is a cargo van without seating rearward of the driver.
heavy_vehicle.source_citation: Instructions for Form 4562, Part I, 'Section 179 deduction for SUVs'; IRC 179(b)(5); IRS Pub. 946 ch. 5

residential_rental.label: Residential rental building
residential_rental.note: A building where 80% or more of gross rental income is from dwelling units. Mid-month convention, straight line. Land is never depreciable.
residential_rental.source_citation: IRS Pub. 946 (2025), ch. 4 '8. Residential rental property' and Appendix A, Table A-6

nonresidential.label: Nonresidential building
nonresidential.note: Office buildings, stores, warehouses. Mid-month convention, straight line over 39 years. Land is never depreciable.
nonresidential.source_citation: IRS Pub. 946 (2025), ch. 4 '9. Nonresidential real property' and Appendix A, Table A-7a

land_improvements.label: Land improvements
land_improvements.note: Fences, roads, sidewalks, parking lots, shrubbery. 15-year, 150% declining balance. Not section 179 property (section 1250 property).
land_improvements.source_citation: IRS Pub. 946 (2025), ch. 4 '15-year property' (a.) and Table 4-1 (GDS using 150% DB: all 15-year property)

qualified_production.label: Qualified production property (Sec. 168(n))
qualified_production.note: The production portion of a nonresidential building. If you elect section 168(n) and the construction and placed-in-service dates qualify, 100% of the designated basis is deductible in the first year; otherwise it is ordinary 39-year property.
qualified_production.source_citation: Notice 2026-16; IRC 168(n); IRS Pub. 946 (2025) Table A-7a for the non-elected basis

other.label: Other (choose the recovery period)
other.note: Tangible personal property with a recovery period you have determined from Pub. 946 Appendix B.
other.source_citation: IRS Pub. 946 (2025), ch. 4 'Which Property Class Applies Under GDS?' and Table 4-1
